acceptance_criteria: AC-1 A Check Point and a Palo Alto configuration job each run end to end against a fake transport and record exactly what 14G CG-3/CG-6 describe, including override rows for src=local; a worker death mid-run leaves no partial run.
AC-2 The four configuration routes have direct backend tests covering their shapes and every status code they return.
AC-3 The artefact store is backed by a PersistentVolumeClaim in the manifests, asserted by tests/test_ui2_deployment_manifests.py, mounted only by the worker.
AC-4 HA role (physical and per-VSID) and VLAN id are persisted by V17 and shown per context in the inventory read model and screen, for both vendors.

AC-5 Eleven-module build, worker/service/persistence/architecture/frontend tests, manifests test, migration-audit-context test, privacy gate and contract_authority_status green; the four queue items are updated through the tool.

baseline.what_exists: Merged (PR 296): worker.configuration with ConfigurationReadPlan (closed literal set, tested), ConfigurationCapabilityExecutor (its constructor defaults panoramaCrossCheck to PanoramaCrossCheckPort.NONE), CheckPointGaiaConfigProcessor, PaloAltoConfigStreamProcessor, ConfigurationJobExecutor, persistence device_configuration_run / _index / _override / panorama_assignment / configuration_notification / configuration_artefact (V16), FileArtefactStore + ArtefactStoreCipher (one master key, streamed AES-256-GCM, content-addressed), ConfigurationController and the Configuration screen. Its tests cover processors, repository, gate alignment and the frontend, but there is NO ConfigurationJobExecutorEndToEndTest / WorkerDiesTest and no backend test for the controller or its services. The pattern to copy is worker.inventory's own InventoryJobExecutor tests (end-to-end against a scripted fake DeviceTransport, plus a worker-dies test) and InventoryControllerTest. deploy/ui2/52-worker-deployment.yaml mounts the artefact store at /app/artefact-store from an emptyDir (see the comment near the UI2_ARTEFACT_STORE_PATH env). Inventory: CheckPointHaStateParser exposes perVsidLocalRole() and the cluster mode; CheckPointIpAddrParser reads the VLAN id from the 'vlan protocol 802.1Q id <n>' detail line and from a 'name.ID@parent' header; device_inventory_run / device_interface / device_route (V13) carry no column for either. Migration V17 is free.

report.objective: Close the three gaps movement NXS-LOCAL-0165 disclosed in its own SESSION_CLOSE rather than leaving them to rot: (1) no end-to-end configuration job test for either vendor, and no backend test for the configuration routes; (2) the artefact store's volume is an emptyDir, so a worker restart loses artefacts while device_configuration_run rows still point at them by artefact_ref; (3) the inventory worker parses HA role and VLAN id and then throws them away because no column exists. All three are known, written-down debts of merged work, not new scope.
output_contract: The configuration and inventory services proved end to end, their artefacts durable, HA role and VLAN visible.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every new type or column names the clause it serves (14G CG-n, 14C D-n, 14D PR-4, C7 section n).
Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'. Do not run the full Python pytest suite; run the named files. Eleven Gradle subprojects. Migration V17 only, additive.
No estate value in fixtures, logs, audit rows or error messages; the multi-megabyte fixture is generated in the test, never checked in.

A migration that writes a row to an audited table must set app.actor_fingerprint and app.action_id transaction-locally first -- tests/test_migration_audit_context.py enforces it and two rollouts crash-looped without it.
If a contract clause and this packet disagree, raise a RELAY_QUESTION and STOP; mechanical mismatches are settled against the code per the standing rules.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.
Open the PR at the end; do not merge. SESSION_CLOSE names the tests added, the claim manifest, the V17 columns and the queue items closed, with test counts before and after.
risks: Checking a multi-megabyte fixture into the repository.
Turning the end-to-end test into a second implementation of the processor rather than a proof of the executor.
Changing the artefact path or its env name while moving to a claim.
Writing HA role onto the device row instead of the run-scoped table, which would lose per-context truth.

in: End-to-end configuration tests, in the exact shape of worker.inventory's: ConfigurationJobExecutorEndToEndTest for Check Point (fixture in the measured shape: a few hundred set lines, a handful of secret-bearing ones, the '#' header) asserting one run recorded with the canonical hash over set lines, the withheld count, the section index and both artefacts; the same for Palo Alto with a synthetic multi-megabyte effective-running generated in the test, asserting the category index per vsys, the override rows for src=local elements and the gzip+encrypted artefact; a ConfigurationJobExecutorWorkerDiesTest asserting no partial run survives a lease lapse.

Backend tests for the routes, in InventoryControllerTest's shape: ConfigurationControllerTest and ConfigurationQueryService / ConfigurationCollectService tests with fakes, covering the four routes' shapes and status codes including the 404s and the 409 when a device has no run.

Artefact durability: replace the emptyDir with a PersistentVolumeClaim (a new deploy/ui2 manifest in the numbering already used, modest size, ReadWriteOnce) mounted at the same path in the worker Deployment; extend tests/test_ui2_deployment_manifests.py so the artefact path is asserted to come from a claim, not an emptyDir, and so every other writable path keeps its existing assertion. The service role does not mount it. Add one line to docs/operations/UI2_LOCAL_KUBERNETES_DEPLOYMENT.md about the claim.

Inventory HA role and VLAN: migration V17 adding, additively, device_inventory_run-scoped HA facts (a small device_inventory_ha table keyed by run and context: role, cluster_mode, source) and a vlan_id column on device_interface; the Check Point executor writes the physical role, the cluster mode and the per-VSID roles the VSLS table yields (14D PR-4), and the VLAN id where the parser found one; the Palo Alto executor writes the HA state it already reads and the tag as vlan_id; the read model and the Inventory screen show the HA role per context and the VLAN id column. Repository, service and frontend tests follow the existing patterns.
